reason: Not refuted as a zero-cost, read-only calibration text: no kernel, slot, runtime or finals effect; R1-R10 untouched; not a closed line. The forecast/calibration logic is sound: the board orders by unrounded score and exact ties by earlier submission (round 11 record (3)), and copies sorting by time inside the public 0.953 block already show that copies are deterministic. Three defects must be fixed before recording. (1) STALE PREMISE: the 20:33Z user decision (commit 620f718) and ladder rule L9 (reach0955/r_ladder.json) can change the finals to {V*, #38}, with V* submitted 26 Sep 21Z or later. R12P-3 hard-codes max(k37,k38), the 26 Sep 00:02Z timestamp and a 16:54 forecast made for {#37,#38}. (2) Read (b) merges two cases. Inside the copy run (after the earlier copies, before the later ones) means exactly = X. Below the whole run means < X. (3) Read (d) is confounded and quantised: private scores show only 3 decimals, and public margins of 0.002-0.004 give per-team ratio steps of 0.25-0.5, so a median cannot separate 0.3 from 0.5. Rivals' private is also the max of their own selected pair. Value is calibration only (zero outcome value), which the finding admits.
fix: Record in CONTEXT/LESSONS s5 as 'confounded, calibration only' with these edits. (i) Our result = the max over the pair ACTUALLY in API SELECTED at 29 Sep 20:00Z, using that file's own submit time. If the pair is not {#37,#38}, append a dated re-issued forecast before 29 Sep 23:59Z, or label (e) 'forecast was for a different pair'. (ii) (b) three cases: above every earlier exact copy -> unrounded max > X; between the earlier and later copies -> = X; below the whole run -> < X. (iii) Replace (d) with the unrounded-order read: the fraction of public-0.955-0.957 teams (from the R12P-4 snapshot) whose private rank is above the X copy run, plus their median rank change; no ratio. (iv) Keep 'one draw, no rule'. Keep API reads sparse (429s at 20:36Z).
